name: SpaceX candidate site 9 (same spot as AP-9)
Prime site, rated safest (NASA/SpaceX study)
source: Golombek et al. 2021, 'SpaceX Starship Landing Sites on Mars', LPSC 52 abstract 2420 (NASA JPL with SpaceX), Table 1: 39.8°N, 202.1°E. 'AP-1 appears to be the safest site and has a moderate combined SWIM score for ice.' Also Luzzi et al. 2023 (LPSC 54, abstract 2335) and 2025 (JGR Planets, doi 10.1029/2024JE008724): ice about 6-20 cm deep.

name: Secondary site, first choice (NASA/SpaceX study)
source: Golombek et al. 2021, 'SpaceX Starship Landing Sites on Mars', LPSC 52 abstract 2420 (NASA JPL with SpaceX), Table 1: 40.75°N, 201.3°E. Next to the sinuous unit; 'AP-8 appears the safest and has the highest neutron and combined SWIM scores for ice' of three sites over the thick-ice radar reflector. Also Luzzi et al. 2023, 2025.

name: Prime site, thickest ice (NASA/SpaceX study)
source: Golombek et al. 2021, 'SpaceX Starship Landing Sites on Mars', LPSC 52 abstract 2420 (NASA JPL with SpaceX), Table 1: 40.02°N, 203.35°E. 'AP-9 has the thickest ice from radar returns ... the highest combined SWIM score for ice, but appears slightly rocky and rough.' Also Luzzi et al. 2023, 2025; HiRISE ESP_060811_2205 is centred here.

name: Prime site by Erebus Montes ice-rich apron (NASA/SpaceX study)
source: Golombek et al. 2021, 'SpaceX Starship Landing Sites on Mars', LPSC 52 abstract 2420 (NASA JPL with SpaceX), Table 1: 39.89°N, 192.03°E. On a lobate debris apron (buried glacier ice); 'a clear association with an LDA'. Near SpaceX candidate site 4.

name: Secondary site by Erebus Montes (NASA/SpaceX study)
source: Golombek et al. 2021, 'SpaceX Starship Landing Sites on Mars', LPSC 52 abstract 2420 (NASA JPL with SpaceX), Table 1: 39.75°N, 195.62°E. Second choice of the three secondary sites; next to a less extensive debris apron. Near SpaceX candidate site 5.
